ADA-S2-2026.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 2. Diagnosis and Classification of Diabetes: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026;49(Suppl 1):S27–S49.
ADA-S2-2026.supports: Diagnostic cut-offs: A1C 6.5% or above; fasting plasma glucose 126 mg/dL or above; 2-h plasma glucose 200 mg/dL or above on a 75 g OGTT; random glucose with classic symptoms. Prediabetes: A1C 5.7–6.4%, fasting glucose 100–125 mg/dL, 2-h glucose 140–199 mg/dL. Confirmatory testing is required without unequivocal hyperglycaemia. Screening for type 2 and prediabetes (Table 2.5 and recs. 2.11–2.13): test all adults from age 35 and repeat at least every 3 years; below that age test adults with overweight or obesity — BMI 25 kg/m2 or above, or 23 kg/m2 or above for individuals of Asian ancestry — who have one or more listed risk factors, high-risk ancestry among them.

ADA-S6-2026.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 6. Glycemic Goals, Hypoglycemia, and Hyperglycemic Crises: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026;49(Suppl 1):S132–S149.
ADA-S6-2026.supports: Hypoglycaemia levels: level 1 below 70 and at or above 54 mg/dL; level 2 below 54 mg/dL; level 3 defined by needing assistance. Written for people with diabetes. The same section covers hyperglycaemic crises — diabetic ketoacidosis and the hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state — as medical emergencies.

CDC-DKA.citation: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Diabetic Ketoacidosis.
CDC-DKA.supports: DKA signs: great thirst, frequent urination, fast deep breathing, fruity-smelling breath, nausea and vomiting, stomach pain, tiredness. It can be the first sign of undiagnosed diabetes. Severe symptoms can appear quickly; it is an emergency.

PHILHEALTH-KONSULTA.citation: Philippine Health Insurance Corporation. Annex B: Konsulta Benefit Table. PhilHealth Circular 2024-0013.
PHILHEALTH-KONSULTA.supports: The primary care package lists fasting blood sugar, oral glucose tolerance test and HbA1c among its laboratory examinations, as needed and on the primary care team's assessment. Renamed YAKAP in 2025. A test may be done at a partner laboratory rather than on site.

DOH-NHFR.citation: Department of Health, Republic of the Philippines. National Health Facility Registry.
DOH-NHFR.supports: The official master list of health facilities. Located but NOT queried facility by facility in this build.

ADA-S3-2026.citation: American Diabetes Association Professional Practice Committee. 3. Prevention or Delay of Diabetes and Associated Comorbidities: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026. Diabetes Care. 2026;49(Suppl 1):S50–S60.
ADA-S3-2026.supports: Referral of adults with overweight or obesity at high risk of type 2 diabetes to a diabetes prevention programme targeting a weight reduction of at least 5–7% (rec. 3.3); offering prevention programmes to adults at high risk (rec. 3.5); greater benefit with 7–10% weight loss; metformin considered in defined higher-risk groups (rec. 3.7).

DPP-2002.citation: Knowler WC, Barrett-Connor E, Fowler SE, et al. Reduction in the incidence of type 2 diabetes with lifestyle intervention or metformin. N Engl J Med. 2002;346(6):393–403.
DPP-2002.supports: The trial behind the prevention recommendation: an intensive lifestyle intervention reduced the incidence of type 2 diabetes by about 58% and metformin by about 31%, against placebo, over a mean of roughly 3 years.
